scope: A second new auction run end to end through the hosted live demo on public Zcash testnet, by the author in an ordinary browser on Oct 28: create, four sealed demo bids, deposits, REP3/coNoir clearing at a fresh price of 30, native shielded settlement with six Halo2 output bindings and 2-of-3 FROST, public verification, and a losing bidder's shielded refund decrypted with its own viewing key.
host: https://49-12-250-128.sslip.io/demo/run (one Linux server; every role, including each demo bidder's client, runs on it)
driven_by: the author, clicking through the live site in a browser; no script

auction.bids: demo bids typed by the author; not recorded here (the price 30 is the highest losing bid by the auction rule)

chain.settlement_on_explorer: https://testnet.zecblock.com/tx/9d0869fa21ec41d2770284310f2c1292b69be513316ab0376269063f63382976: block 4,552,260, 6 Ironwood actions, fee 0.0003 TAZ, 21,790 bytes; 28 confirmations when looked up at 22:18 UTC

stages_seconds.funding_note: deposits confirmed, then the operators waited for the declared 600 s funding deadline, rescanned and signed the book again over the same root: 4 client proofs, 12 share pairs, 12 receipt signatures, 3 final-book signatures
stages_seconds.settlement_note: fresh REP3 delivery on the same shares, six Halo2 output bindings (about 73 s each), 2-of-3 FROST signing, broadcast and two confirmations

checks.public_verification: native row proofs verified and accepted book certified (the server's public verifier, no viewing key)
checks.own_receipt: a losing ticket's shielded receipt decrypted with that ticket's viewing key only: no unit, refund 100 zatoshi, the full budget
checks.source: the server's own progress records for this auction (funding and settlement phases, with times) and the page the author saw

why_it_matters: A different price from the recorded Oct 19 auction (21): the outcome was computed from new bids, not replayed. It is the second new auction through the hosted site after Oct 27 (03feb02b…9cf72d8b).
limits: Demo bids and one funding wallet on the server; the server runs every bidder client and all three semi-honest REP3 parties.
